meaning: The EC2 market where AWS can take an instance back after a two-minute warning sent on a best-effort basis; open to jobs that lose little when a machine goes.
The regular EC2 market, where an instance runs until you stop it.
A model in which a vision-language model reads the camera images and the instruction and an action head attached to it outputs the robot's motions.
The vision-language model a VLA is built on; the part that reads images and text.
The part of a VLA that turns the backbone's output into the arm's motions.
One update of a model's weights during training, computed from one batch.
One moment of a recorded episode, camera images and joint angles paired with the actions that followed, as training reads it.
The samples one training step processes; the per-GPU batch is what one GPU holds, the global batch is that times the number of GPUs.
For each weight that trains, the direction in which a step moves it; it occupies GPU memory alongside the weight.
The running statistics the optimiser keeps for each weight that trains, from step to step; a frozen weight has none.
The intermediate values the forward pass computes for each sample, kept in GPU memory until the backward pass uses them; they grow with the batch.
A training switch that recomputes activations in the backward pass in place of storing them, trading compute for GPU memory.
Said of weights that training reads but does not update, so they need no gradient or optimiser state.
Further training that updates every weight of a pretrained model.
The published configuration of a training run: the model, the batch, the number of steps and which weights train.
A fine-tune that freezes the base weights and trains small matrices added beside them, which cuts the memory a fine-tune needs.
A fine-tuning setting that leaves the vision-language model untouched and trains only the action head and the layer that feeds it.
The part of the backbone that turns camera images into vectors.
Training on several GPUs where each keeps a copy of the model, works through its own share of the batch, and the copies combine their gradients into one update per step.
Data-parallel training that splits the weights, gradients and optimiser state across the GPUs in place of a full copy on each, for models whose trainable state does not fit one GPU.
The number of GPUs a job holds multiplied by the hours it holds them; occupied GPU time, not work, since GPU models differ.
The first training of a model, on data from many robots or on video, before it has seen the reader's robot.
Any training that starts from a pretrained checkpoint; its size varies from one GPU to several servers.
A saved copy of a model's weights; during a run, also the saved state the run resumes from after a stop.
One pass of training over every frame of the dataset.
One server in a training job, such as an EC2 instance with eight GPUs.
A CPU process that reads, decodes and prepares samples into batches for the GPU.
EC2's unit of processor capacity, one hardware thread; most eight-GPU sizes carry 24 per GPU.
A 2-byte number format for model weights; NVIDIA lists GR00T N1.7 in it.
A small policy of about 80M parameters that predicts a chunk of actions per look and is trained from scratch on one task.
Training in which the policy improves from scored attempts, here in a simulator.
Meta's action-conditioned predictor trained on top of its V-JEPA 2 video encoder, on under 62 hours of robot video with the encoder frozen.
A SageMaker service that starts instances for one training job and shuts them down when it ends.
The SageMaker Training Jobs setting that runs a job on Spot, copies its checkpoints to S3 and back, and resumes after an interruption; it does not fall back to On-Demand.
AWS's persistent training cluster, deployed in one Availability Zone by default.
AWS's managed Lustre, a file system many processes read in parallel, used to keep data and checkpoints between training jobs.
AWS's managed Kubernetes; its best-practices guide gives the checkpoint intervals cited here.
The EC2 network device for traffic between instances that bypasses the operating system kernel so many machines can train as one; absent on small GPU sizes.
One of the separate data-centre groups inside an AWS Region; EFA traffic cannot cross from one to another.
An EC2 setting that packs instances close together on the network; AWS Batch requires one for EFA jobs.
A SageMaker HyperPod feature, built on NVIDIA NeMo, that rebuilds a failed node's training state from its healthy peers instead of restarting from a saved checkpoint.
A HyperPod feature for PyTorch on EKS that keeps checkpoints in the nodes' CPU memory, copies them to adjacent nodes and periodically persists them to durable storage such as S3.
Large simulation and scientific jobs run across many servers that exchange data as they compute; AWS's HPC team tested such a job on Spot.
An open-source job scheduler for clusters, the one AWS's HPC Spot test ran under.
NVIDIA's training framework, on which checkpointless training is built.
An EC2 reservation of P or Trainium instances for a set window; no G family is offered.
A SageMaker reservation of P or Trainium capacity for 1 to 182 days, bookable up to 8 weeks ahead.
